eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecasts from multiple meteorological sources converge on a daytime high of 24–25°C for Mexico City on August 20, 2026, aligning with the market’s leading implied probabilities (25°C at 46.5%, 24°C at 28.5%).** 

August falls within the peak of the North American monsoon and Mexico’s rainy season, when afternoon convective showers and increased cloud cover routinely cap maximum temperatures near the long-term average of roughly 24°C (75°F). Mexico City’s elevation of approximately 2,240 m further moderates readings, preventing the extreme heat seen at lower elevations. Current model guidance and extended outlooks (AccuWeather, timeanddate, BBC) show overcast or showery conditions with highs in the mid-70s °F (24–25°C), consistent with historical climatology that rarely exceeds 26–27°C in mid-August without a strong subsidence event. 

Traders appear to weight the high likelihood of typical monsoon-driven cloudiness and precipitation against only modest upside potential from clearer intervals, producing the tight clustering around 24–26°C. Updated official forecasts from CONAGUA/SMN or late-day observational data could shift probabilities if skies clear earlier than expected.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Current short-range ensemble forecasts and official guidance from IMGW and agencies such as the Met Office and BBC point to a maximum of 25–26 °C in Warsaw on 21 August 2026, with light south-westerly flow, partly cloudy skies, and limited diurnal heating keeping the peak moderate.** Recent model runs show only small spreads between 24–27 °C depending on the timing of any showers or breaks of sun, which explains why the 26 °C and 27 °C contracts remain closely matched at roughly 35–43 % implied probability. Traders are weighting the upper end of the guidance range because afternoon insolation under variable cloud can still push readings 1–2 °C higher than the headline forecast maximum. No major warm-air advection or clear-sky setup is expected to support 28 °C or higher, while cooler outcomes below 25 °C would require more persistent cloud or stronger winds than currently modeled. Final resolution rests on the official IMGW station reading at noon the following day, so any last-minute shift in the 00 UTC or 12 UTC runs could quickly reprice the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: The southwest monsoon (Habagat) and associated cloud cover plus scattered showers remain the dominant factors capping Manila's peak temperatures near 30–32°C for August 22. Official PAGASA guidance and extended outlooks show daytime maxima of 32°C with 60–70% rain probability, consistent with climatological August averages of 30–31°C under humid, convective conditions. These patterns suppress insolation and promote evaporative cooling, reducing the likelihood of brief clear-sky spikes above 33°C. Market-implied odds cluster tightly around 30–32°C, reflecting trader weighting of stable monsoon steering and minimal model spread in short-range forecasts; any unexpected break in cloudiness or delayed rainfall could shift probabilities toward the upper end of that range before resolution.
